description: A chess engine that plays from a learned evaluation, with its Python trainer, built on esca: a chess model that answers what is true about a position (variants, positions, games, move text, and a versioned schema of position facts) as a Rust crate and a Python package
rules: esca is the published part: `esca = "0.1"` in Cargo.toml, or `pip install esca` for the abi3-py312 wheel built from the same crate. The engine crate anglerfish-core and the pyanglerfish trainer are not published.

A Position is placement and state only; the rules are a Variant (Classic, Chess960), and a Game is a variant plus the moves played — repetition and claimable draws need the history, so they live on Game, not Position.

Facts answers what is true about a position in nine groups (state, material, pawns, pieces, king, mobility, attacks, tactics, planes) plus MoveFacts per legal move. Everything is side-relative and in the mover's view: index pairs with Side::Us/Side::Them in Rust, esca.US/esca.THEM in Python.

Schema::v0 (esca.SCHEMA_V0) is the versioned contract between the extractor and the net: 1065 f32 columns, identified by a schema_id that golden fixtures pin. Encode with facts.encode(schema, schema.all()) in Rust, esca.encode(fens) or esca.encode_into(fens, out) in Python.
Cargo features are off by default: `lichess` is the streaming reader for the Lichess evaluation dump, `python` is the PyO3 module maturin builds the wheel from.
cozy-chess is an implementation detail: no cozy_chess type appears in esca's public API in either language.
MIT-licensed, and so is every dependency; GPL chess libraries are deliberately not used.
